q-142871:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡x\text{ }\,({sec}^{2}⁡x-2{tan}^{2}⁡x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡x\text{ }\,(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x-2{tan}^{2}⁡x) \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x(1-{tan}^{2}⁡x) \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the identities:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},\,{cos}^{2}⁡x=1-{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

 

Using the above identities, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x\text{ }\,({sec}^{2}⁡x-2{tan}^{2}⁡x)=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

q-146313:
Suppose $a$ and $b$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $a\times b=0$ if and only if $a∥b.$

Therefore, $a\times b=0.$

q-146263:
Suppose $a$ and $b$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $a\times b=0$ if and only if $a∥b.$

Since the angle between $a$ and $b$ is ${0}^{∘},$ our vectors must be parallel. 

Therefore, $a\times b=0.$

q-23602:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

q-119904:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡z={csc}^{2}⁡z,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡z\,({cot}^{2}⁡z+1) & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡z \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡z})}^{2} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡z} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡z}{{sin}^{2}⁡z} \\  & ={(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡z})}^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡z\end{aligned}
$$

q-23849:
First, we operate the first two terms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cot}^{2}⁡x}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{({cot}^{2}⁡x-{csc}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{-({csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-({csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{-1}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-{sin}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-65518:
First, we multiply the numerator and the denominator of our expression by $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1.$ This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta $, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\cancel{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{\cancel{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1) \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-23898:
First, we write the given expression as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -\frac{1}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor out ${tan}^{2}⁡\theta $ and use the identity 
${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta .$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,({csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1) \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{cot}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-23897:
First, we use the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta +{cot}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta  & =[1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ]+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta +{cot}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor out ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ and we use the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta $ again. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{2}⁡\theta +{cot}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta  & ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta (1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta \,({csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\, \\  & ={csc}^{4}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
